tools.name: build_private_local_testing_config
tools.description: Build a private local testing configuration payload. IMPORTANT (mode="tunnel"): before calling this tool you MUST have already shown the user an ask_user_questions form (tag "Select Tunnel") with these options: - "Auto-select tunnel (recommended)" - "Tunnel: <id> (started by <username>)" ← one per active tunnel and waited for an explicit selection. Never call this tool to infer a tunnel selection on the user's behalf. Pass selected_tunnel=None for auto-select or selected_tunnel=<id> for a specific tunnel chosen by the user.

include_api_calls.description: Whether API calls should be allowed through the tunnel. Defaults to False when omitted.

selected_tunnel.description: Specific tunnel ID to use. Leave unset to auto-select.

tools.name: build_run_configuration
tools.description: Build a configuration object suitable for create_test_run(mode="automated"). Choose config_type from the requested execution environment, not the suite name. When creating the run, use that same value for automated.test_run_type and pass this configuration in automated.configurations. A suite named API can still be requested to run in a desktop/mobile browser: use DESKTOP_AND_MOBILE_BROWSER then. For TestCloud browsers first call list_test_cloud_environments, e.g. {"rsql_filter": "platform==windows and browser==firefox", "size": 20}. Copy platform -> os, platformVersion -> os_version, browser -> browser, browserVersion -> browser_version, browserVersionType -> browser_version_type from the SAME row. Example: build_run_configuration(config_type= "DESKTOP_AND_MOBILE_BROWSER", os="windows", browser="firefox", browser_version="latest"). Examples are illustrative, not current availability. On INVALID_ENVIRONMENT, use compatibleConfigurations and the suggested lookup to correct the tuple within the user's constraints, then retry create_test_run. For LOCAL_AGENT use list_test_cloud_agents and the agent's installed browser. **Mobile browser vs mobile app selection**: - If the user selects a mobile device but provides no uploaded app information, build a DESKTOP_AND_MOBILE_BROWSER configuration for a mobile browser run. - Ask whether they want mobile browser or mobile app only when their intent is ambiguous. - Use MOBILE_NATIVE only when the user explicitly wants a mobile app run and uploaded app information is available or can be selected. **For MOBILE_NATIVE configs**: First call `list_test_cloud_environments` and `list_test_cloud_apps`, then extract values from their responses. MOBILE_NATIVE requires uploaded app information; do not create a MOBILE_NATIVE config without app ID/name/platform. | This param | From list_test_cloud_environments | From list_test_cloud_apps | |------------|-----------------------------------|---------------------------| | device_name | Use device.deviceName as-is, do NOT add OS version | - | | device_family | device.formFactor (e.g. "PHONE") | - | | device_id | device.deviceId (e.g. "iphone_15_pro") | - | | device_pool | capabilities.automation.devicePoolType | - | | os | platform (e.g. "ios", "android") | - | | os_version | platformVersion as-is (e.g. "17.5") | - | | app_id | - | id | | app_name | - | name | | app_platform | - | platform | | app_version | - | version | | app_version_code | - | versionCode | **Device selection**: - If user specifies device: use that device name in filter - If user says "any iphone" or "any iPhone" (case-insensitive): filter for exact device name "Any iPhone" in list_test_cloud_environments - If user says "any phone" or "any android" (case-insensitive): filter for exact device name "Any Phone" in list_test_cloud_environments - If user doesn't specify any device: default to "Any iPhone" for iOS or "Any Phone" for Android from list_test_cloud_environments - Extract ALL fields directly from API response, do NOT derive or combine For desktop browsers, an unspecified channel defaults to stable and an unspecified browser version defaults to latest within the requested OS/version. Several browser versions in the catalog do not require user confirmation. For mobile devices, ask only when distinct device choices remain ambiguous after applying the user's constraints; do not silently substitute a different device.

agent_type.description: Agent type. For LOCAL_AGENT, supply agent_id.

app_id.description: Uploaded application ID for MOBILE_NATIVE. Required for mobile app runs; omit and use DESKTOP_AND_MOBILE_BROWSER for mobile browser runs.

browser.description: Browser name (chrome, firefox, safari, etc). Required for browser configs.

browser_type.description: Derived from browser when omitted (firefox -> FIREFOX, msedge -> EDGE_CHROMIUM). Explicit values must match browser; mobile uses ALL.

browser_version.description: Exact browserVersion from a compatible catalog row, or latest within the selected OS/version/channel. If no browser version was requested, omit or use latest. Do not copy os_version here. Local and mobile latest remain sentinels.

config_type.description: Choose from the user's requested execution environment, not the suite name. DESKTOP_AND_MOBILE_BROWSER for any desktop/mobile browser, including headless or phones/tablets without uploaded apps, even if the suite name contains API. Native mobile-app testing requires an explicitly requested app and uploaded app information; web-service testing has no browser or device request. Use this same value for create_test_run.automated.test_run_type.

device_id.description: Unique device identifier supplied by TestCloud.

device_name.description: Exact device name. Required for mobile configs.

headless.description: Run browser tests in headless mode.

is_agent_active.description: Flag used for API configurations or LOCAL_AGENT metadata.

name.description: Optional configuration name (API).

os.description: Operating system (ios, android, windows, linux, etc).

os_version.description: Operating system version (e.g., 11 or 14.5). Required for mobile configs.

tools.name: build_schedule
tools.description: Build a schedule payload with timing metadata for create_test_run. For scheduled automated runs, resolve the automated test suite or test-suite collection, execution profile, and run configuration first, then build the schedule and call create_test_run(mode="automated", schedule=...). Do not collect AUT/manual AI fields for automated schedules; schedule controls timing only. For scheduled manual runs, call read_auts and ask the user to choose an AUT environment before building the schedule.

active.description: Whether the schedule should be active. Omit or set True to activate immediately.

days.description: List of days for weekly schedules (e.g., ['MONDAY', 'FRIDAY']).

end_time.description: Optional end time in ISO 8601 format with timezone offset (e.g., '2026-04-06T23:59:59+07:00').

interval.description: Interval for recurring schedules. Required when repeat_enable=True.

interval_unit.description: Interval unit (HOUR, DAY, WEEK, MONTH). Required when repeat_enable=True.

repeat_enable.description: Enable recurring schedule. Omit or set False to disable.

start_time.description: Start time in ISO 8601 format with timezone offset (e.g., '2026-03-31T14:00:00+07:00' for Asia/Saigon). After building the schedule, pass it to create_test_run(mode='automated', schedule=...) for automated runs.

tools.name: confirm_artifact_upload
tools.description: Confirm that a prepared file upload is complete; does not attach evidence. Use the exact artifact ID returned by prepare_artifact_upload, never invent one. After confirmation, pass only {"artifact_id": "<returned ID>"} in update_test_results step evidence. Repeat confirmation is safe: an already-active response is verified by reading the exact version. For a project artifact, keep the same project in the client's request headers. Account artifacts do not require a project header. Confirmation preserves the artifact's original scope. No automatic expiration promised.

tools.name: create_defect
tools.description: Create a new bug or defect in Jira or Azure DevOps (ADO) and link it to a test result. This tool creates a new bug/defect using the configured alm integration (e.g., Jira, Ado) and associates it with a test result. The defect will contain: - Issue type: Bug - Summary (required) - Description (optional) Inputs: - project_id: ID of the project. - alm_integration_id: ID of the configured Alm integration project. - alm_connection_id: ID of the configured Alm connection. - test_result_id: ID of the test result that the defect will be linked to. - payload: Object containing defect metadata. Payload fields: - summary (string, required): Short title describing the defect. - description (string, optional): Detailed explanation of the defect. Usage examples: Create a defect with summary only: payload={ "summary": "Login button does not respond" } Create a defect with summary and description: payload={ "summary": "Checkout fails with 500 error", "description": "When clicking checkout, the API returns a 500 error. Happens consistently on staging." } Create a defect linked to a failed test result: payload={ "summary": "Search API returns incorrect results", "description": "The search endpoint returns unrelated items when filtering by category." } The created defect will automatically be linked to the provided test_result_id. The response includes a URL where the defect can be viewed in the external issue tracker.

alm_connection_id.description: ID of the ALM connection (e.g., Jira, Azure DevOps). If unknown, call list_alm_integrations to retrieve available integration and connection IDs.

alm_integration_id.description: ID of the ALM integration (e.g., Jira, Azure DevOps). If unknown, call list_alm_integrations to retrieve available IDs.

payload.description: Object-based payload containing all metadata fields of the new defect.

description.description: Detailed description of the defect. If the description is unknown or not provided, use the error message from the test result. If no explicit error message is available, generate a meaningful description based on the test result failure information.

summary.description: Summary or title of the defect. Must explicitly ask the user to fill the summary/title if it is missing. Suggest using the failed test case name as the summary. Or use 'Defect for {test case name}' as the default summary when the summary is not provided and the test case name is available.

project_id.description: ID of the project. If not in context, call list_projects to find available options.

test_result_id.description: ID of the test result. If unknown, call find_test_results to retrieve available IDs.

tools.name: create_manual_ai_session
tools.description: Legacy/subset AI-session launcher; use update_test_run for the full TestPak lifecycle. For a full TestPak, use update_test_run START/KATALON_AI, poll read_manual_ai_session, then observe auto-end or call update_test_run END. Do not call this tool before or after that START on the same run. This compatibility tool is for an explicitly selected subset on a fresh run or an older workflow. Existing sessions or results reject a new launch before any configuration write. Reuse the existing session instead of restarting. A failed launch may have committed; inspect state before any retry. Returns sessionId and conversationId for monitoring. Also returns executionPath (relative path on the TestOps/Katalon True Platform web app) when execution_id is provided; omitted otherwise. Supports multiple test suites in a single session. To run every test case in a suite, pass the suite metadata from read_test_suite without a testCases field. Include testCases only for an explicit user-requested subset; do not pick a representative test case for a suite-level request. Use read_manual_ai_session to poll the session progress after triggering. IMPORTANT: Launching a session reuses the run's existing AUT and private access. Omit aut_environment_id, default_aut_environment_url, and private_local_testing_configuration when preserving the current configuration, including settings already applied by create_test_run(mode="manual"). Do not call read_auts, resend the existing AUT, or ask about private access merely to start a session. These optional parameters are configuration overrides and cause an additional write before launch. Use them only for an explicit user-requested change on a fresh run. For an AUT change, select environments[].id from the latest read_auts result; never reuse an AUT from another run. If no configured AUT exists and the user supplies an HTTP(S) URL, use default_aut_environment_url. A requested private access change must use the exact output from build_private_local_testing_config. IMPORTANT: Before starting Run With AI, ask the user to choose a browser profile: "SHARED" reuses cookies, storage, and login state across test cases; "SEPARATE" starts every test case with a clean, isolated browser profile. Do not infer or silently default this choice. Wait for the user's selection, then pass it as browser_profile_mode. IMPORTANT: Run With AI supports Chrome on Windows or Linux only. Before reusing an existing manual run, verify its execution configuration. If it uses another browser or operating system, do not start an AI session from that run. Create a new manual run with a supported Windows-or-Linux Chrome configuration, then call this tool with the new run's manualExecutionId and testSuites. Explain that other browsers and operating systems are not yet supported by Run With AI. When presenting the result to the user, always render executionPath as a markdown link, e.g. [View Run Details](executionPath).

aut_environment_id.description: Optional AUT configuration override; providing this writes to the test run. Omit to preserve the run's existing AUT, including an AUT already selected in create_test_run(mode='manual'). Do not call read_auts or resend the same AUT merely to launch or recover a session. Only for a user-requested AUT change, use environments[].id from the latest read_auts result. Do not reuse an AUT environment from an earlier run. Requires execution_id.

browser_profile_mode.description: How browser state (cookies, storage, login session) is handled across the test cases in this session. "SHARED" reuses one browser profile for all test cases, so state carries over from one test case to the next — use it for dependent/sequential flows, e.g. when a login test case must set up the session for later ones. "SEPARATE" gives each test case its own clean browser profile with isolated state. Before calling this tool, always ask the user to choose SHARED or SEPARATE; do not infer or silently default the choice.

default_aut_environment_url.description: Optional AUT URL override; omit to preserve the run's existing URL. Use only when read_auts shows no configured AUT environments and the user explicitly mentions an HTTP or HTTPS URL. Requires execution_id. Do not use with aut_environment_id.

execution_id.description: Execution ID (executionId) returned by create_test_run(mode='manual'). Used to build the executionPath in the result. If omitted, executionPath will be absent.

manual_execution_id.description: Manual execution ID (manualExecutionId) returned by create_test_run(mode='manual').

os.description: Operating system explicitly selected by the user for Run With AI. Ask the user to choose Windows or Linux; never infer or silently default this value.

private_local_testing_configuration.description: Optional private access override; omit to preserve the run's existing configuration. For a user-requested change, use when the AUT is private/internal/localhost or requires tunnel/whitelist access. Must be the exact output from build_private_local_testing_config tool. Do not resend configuration already applied by create_test_run(mode='manual').

project_id.description: Optional TestOps/Katalon True Platform project ID. Falls back to the MCP context project when omitted.

test_suites.description: List of test suites to include in the AI session. Required fields per entry: testSuiteId (int) and testProjectId (int). testSuiteName (str) is optional. testSuitePath (str) is optional and defaults to "Test Suites" when omitted; include it when available from read_test_suite. When following directly from create_test_run(mode='manual') (which returns only testSuiteId and testProjectId), omitting name and path is fine. If read_test_suite was called beforehand, pass testSuiteName and testSuitePath from its response — do not fetch, infer, or fabricate them. Only include testCases when the user explicitly asks to run a subset of cases. Full-suite item: {"testSuiteId": int, "testProjectId": int, "testSuiteName": str (optional), "testSuitePath": str (optional)}. Subset-only item (use only when the user explicitly selected specific cases; these are the only cases that will run): {"testSuiteId": int, "testProjectId": int, "testSuiteName": str (optional), "testSuitePath": str (optional), "testCases": [{"testCaseId": int, "name": str, "testCasePath": str}]}.

tools.name: create_test_case
tools.description: Author one concrete TestOps test case from a specified title or steps. MANUAL creates the manual test case; AUTOMATED returns the next action for executable automation script generation.

project_id.description: ID of the project. If not in context, call list_projects to find available options.

repository_id.description: ID of the repository (Test Project). If unknown, call list_repositories to find available options.

test_case.description: Test case details or automation context. Select the authoring intent with the sibling test_case_type field.

automationStatus.description: Automation status metadata for a persisted manual test case. This field does not select automated authoring; use create_test_case.test_case_type.

steps.description: List of test steps. Every step has a human-readable 'name' and optional 'context' (expected result + data); a step may additionally carry a structured 'action' for automated execution (e.g. Call Test Case — see CreateTestCaseStep.action). Unique IDs are generated automatically when creating the test case.

items.description: Test case step definition for LLM input - ID will be auto-generated when sending to API.

anyOf.description:
Call Test Case step action — invoke a shared/existing test case.

One concrete kind of step action. New action types will be added as sibling
models discriminated on ``type``; keep this pattern when extending.

test_case_id.description: ID of the shared/existing test case this step should call.

version.description: Pin the call to a specific version of the callee. Omit to always call the callee's latest version.

action.description: Optional structured action attached to the step so an automated executor (e.g. AI Test Runner) can perform it — in ADDITION to the human-readable name/context, not instead of it. Discriminated by `type`; today the only type is 'call' (Call Test Case): set {"type": "call", "test_case_id": <id>} (optionally "version": <n>) when the user asks to 'call test case <id>' or reuse a shared flow (e.g. a common Login). Still fill `name` (e.g. 'Login') and, if known, `context` so manual execution works. Do NOT encode a call as a plain manual step named 'Call test case <id>' with no action — the runner then cannot trigger the referenced case. More action types may be added here in future.

data.description: Data associated with the test step

expectedResult.description: Expected result of the test step

context.description:
Context containing expected result and optional test data.

        Expected format (both fields must be strings):
        {
          "expectedResult": "Description of what should happen",
          "data": "Additional test data (can be empty string)"
        }

        Fill this for manual execution regardless of whether the step also has an
        `action` — a manual tester follows name/expectedResult/data.

name.description: Human-readable label/description of the step (e.g. 'Navigate to Login page'). A manual tester reads this; keep it meaningful even when the step also carries a structured `action`.

version.description: Version of the test case content format

customTestTypes.description: User-defined test type for custom classification. Unlike the system testType, this is fully configurable to match internal naming conventions.

featureAreas.description: Specifies the functional areas covered or affected by the test case.

name.description: The name of the test case. Must start with English letters (a-z, A-Z) or numbers (0-9). Can contain spaces and these characters: ( ) . , _ -

path.description:
Folder path (excluding the test case name). Must always start with 'Test Cases' or 'Test Cases/'.
    Example: 'Test Cases/Report_Analytics/Manual Test Cases'

test_case_type.description: Authoring intent. MANUAL creates a manual test case and is the default when automation is not requested. Set AUTOMATED when the user explicitly requests automated/automation test cases or an automation script; it returns automation script generation guidance.

tools.name: create_test_cloud_app
tools.description: Create a TestCloud app from an uploaded app file. This tool allows you to register an uploaded app to TestCloud. If users have uploaded an app from the Testcloud website, skip this tool. If an app is uploaded by UI tool or by execution script need to call this tool to register the uploaded app.

tools.name: create_test_run
tools.description: Create a TestPak (manual test run) or an automated test run in Katalon TestOps/Katalon True Platform. A TestPak request selects mode="manual". Creating a test suite alone does not create a TestPak. For "create a TestPak for later", create the run and return its execution link without calling START. To execute it, use update_test_run START after creation; the selected execution path determines MANUAL or KATALON_AI. "Start/run this TestPak" or "start with TestPak" selects START/MANUAL, including "create a test run ... then start with testPak". An explicit Run With AI/hosted AI request selects START/KATALON_AI. If neither path is selected, ask whether the user wants manual TestPak testing or fully autonomous Run With AI, recommend AI for automatic execution, and wait before START. Do not choose AI because the client lacks browser tools. TestPak holds either execution path; naming the workspace does not authorize an AI session. Manual testing does not need an AI browser-profile choice or AI provisioning checks. Use `mode="manual"` for manual runs. Manual mode supports Run Now when `schedule` is omitted and scheduled manual runs when `schedule` is provided. Before every manual run, call read_auts; ask the user to choose an AUT environment or skip only when that choice is missing. Reuse explicit skip-AUT and no-private-access choices; do not re-confirm them or an explicit TestPak/manual execution path. For Run Now manual runs, the result preserves manualExecutionId and testSuites for update_test_run and read_manual_ai_session. Use `mode="automated"` for Katalon Studio/TestCloud automated runs. Automated mode operates on automated test suites or test suite collections only and never on individual test cases. For scheduled automated runs, use build_schedule once and pass its result as `schedule` while keeping mode="automated"; do not call read_auts, ask for AUT, or collect manual/AI fields. Gather only the automated bundle: test run type, automated suite or collection entries, execution profile, run configuration, and timing/recurrence details. For automated runs, choose the run type from the requested execution environment, not the suite name or entity metadata. Use build_run_configuration with that config_type, then use the same value for automated.test_run_type. A browser/device request uses DESKTOP_AND_MOBILE_BROWSER even if the suite name contains API. Parallelism examples (fields inside automated): - "Run the collection in parallel": execution_mode="PARALLEL", parallelize_test_cases=false. - "Run desktop and mobile browsers at the same time": supply both configurations, parallelize_test_cases=false; omit execution_mode for a single suite. - "Parallelize independent test cases" / "enable true parallel": parallelize_test_cases=true. This is TestCloud's separate test-case-level feature, not collection execution_mode or concurrency across browser/device configurations. User-supplied Additional KRE Arguments go inside automated, for example: additional_kre_arguments='-g_runLabel="nightly smoke"'. Copy the exact supplied string. For testSuiteQuery, use a verified expression for the suite's selected filtering extension; this tool does not preview matching cases. Never drop a requested selector to recover from an error or create a broader run. If the user asks to create a test run without specifying TestPak or another run type, ask whether they want a manual or automated run before calling this tool.

anyOf.description: Payload for create_test_run(mode='automated').

additional_kre_arguments.description: Additional KRE Arguments for Test Execution Cloud. Copy the exact user-supplied string; do not invent query syntax or drop a selector. testSuiteQuery must match the suite's selected filtering extension; this tool does not preview matches. Use profile_id/configurations for managed settings. Omit/null to leave unset.

anyOf.description: A complete environment selection, never a suite-to-environment mapping.

agentId.description: For LOCAL_AGENT, call list_test_cloud_agents and copy the selected item's id. Omit for TEST_CLOUD_AGENT; never invent an agent ID.

agentType.description: Required execution target: TEST_CLOUD_AGENT or LOCAL_AGENT.

appGroupId.description: Preserve an existing value from read_schedule_detail or use an explicit user-supplied value. list_test_cloud_apps does not expose appGroupId, so never invent it.

appId.description: For MOBILE_NATIVE, call list_test_cloud_apps with the user's platform, name, and status constraints, select a READY app, and copy its id. Required for each MOBILE_NATIVE suite environment.

appName.description: Copy name from the selected list_test_cloud_apps item.

appVersion.description: Legacy backend DTO field. Preserve it only when it already exists. For a new MOBILE_NATIVE app selection, the frontend writes app version values to metadata.appVersion and metadata.appVersionCode instead.

browser.description: Call list_test_cloud_environments with every browser, OS, version, and device constraint from the user, then copy the selected item's browser. This is an API browser value (chrome, firefox, safari, edge, msedge, or internet explorer), not a device category. Frontend-only deviceFamily values such as desktop, phone, iPhone, or tablet are lookup filters and must never be translated into browser. Omit this field when a MANUAL or WEB_SERVICE configuration has no selected browser; existing legacy blank values are preserved internally for unrelated updates.

browserType.description: Fixed API category compatible with the selected list_test_cloud_environments item; use the enum value, not a UI label.

browserVersion.description: Exact catalog browserVersion or latest; validated before creation.

deviceId.description: Copy device.deviceId from the selected list_test_cloud_environments item.

deviceName.description: Call list_test_cloud_environments with every mobile constraint and copy the selected item's device.deviceName.

executionType.description: Fixed API category compatible with browserType and the selected list_test_cloud_environments item.

headless.description: Use only for a compatible desktop browser selected through list_test_cloud_environments.

id.description: For an existing configuration, copy this ID from read_schedule_detail. Omit it for a new configuration; never invent it.

anyOf.description: Frontend-authored metadata keys accepted for schedule environments.

appVersion.description: For MOBILE_NATIVE, copy metadata.version from the selected READY list_test_cloud_apps item, matching the frontend payload.

appVersionCode.description: For MOBILE_NATIVE, copy metadata.versionCode from the selected READY list_test_cloud_apps item, matching the frontend payload.

browserVersionType.description: Copy the exact stable, beta, or dev value from the selected list_test_cloud_environments item.

devicePool.description: Copy capabilities.automation.devicePoolType from the selected mobile list_test_cloud_environments item for shared devices. The frontend/catalog values are main_shared_pool, sub_shared_pool, and private_cloud; this is not free text and is never a substitute for frontend-only deviceFamily. The unified environment catalog does not expose private-device UDIDs, so preserve an existing private-cloud UDID or use one explicitly provided by the user. The update tool validates the environment identity and pool against that catalog before PUT.

Preserve private-cloud metadata from read_schedule_detail or use exact user-provided values; the unified environment catalog does not expose private-device UDIDs. Private-cloud devices additionally carry metadata.udid; the tool adds the backend-only metadata.devicePoolId from organization context and validates the environment identity and pool against the unified catalog. For MOBILE_NATIVE, app metadata.version and metadata.versionCode map to metadata.appVersion and metadata.appVersionCode. Frontend display/catalog fields such as deviceFamily are not metadata; do not copy capabilities wholesale or synthesize any other key.

os.description: Call list_test_cloud_environments with every user constraint and copy the selected item's platform value into os.

testCloudEnvironmentUuid.description: Optional backend catalog identity. Preserve the current value or copy an explicit UUID returned by an API that exposes it. The frontend environment builder does not require this field for device-pool selections; never invent it.

agentId.description: For LOCAL_AGENT, call list_test_cloud_agents and copy the selected item's id. Omit for TEST_CLOUD_AGENT; never invent an agent ID.

agentType.description: Required execution target: TEST_CLOUD_AGENT or LOCAL_AGENT.

appGroupId.description: Preserve an existing value from read_schedule_detail or use an explicit user-supplied value. list_test_cloud_apps does not expose appGroupId, so never invent it.

appId.description: For MOBILE_NATIVE, call list_test_cloud_apps with the user's platform, name, and status constraints, select a READY app, and copy its id. Required for each MOBILE_NATIVE suite environment.

appVersion.description: Legacy backend DTO field. Preserve it only when it already exists. For a new MOBILE_NATIVE app selection, the frontend writes app version values to metadata.appVersion and metadata.appVersionCode instead.

browser.description: Call list_test_cloud_environments with every browser, OS, version, and device constraint from the user, then copy the selected item's browser. This is an API browser value (chrome, firefox, safari, edge, msedge, or internet explorer), not a device category. Frontend-only deviceFamily values such as desktop, phone, iPhone, or tablet are lookup filters and must never be translated into browser. Omit this field when a MANUAL or WEB_SERVICE configuration has no selected browser; existing legacy blank values are preserved internally for unrelated updates.

browserType.description: Fixed API category compatible with the selected list_test_cloud_environments item; use the enum value, not a UI label.

browserVersion.description: Exact catalog browserVersion or latest; validated before creation.

tools.name: fetch_defects
tools.description: Fetch defect data for execution test results, test cases, or an execution. Use this tool when the user asks whether defects, issues, or linked tickets exist for execution test results, test cases, or an execution. Supported lookup targets via `filter.filter_type`: - TEST_RESULT: requires `test_result_ids`; fetches defects for exact execution test result IDs. - TEST_CASE: requires `test_case_ids`; optionally accepts `execution_id` to limit the lookup to one execution. Resolves execution test results for those test cases, then fetches linked defects. - EXECUTION: requires `execution_id`; resolves execution test results in that execution, then fetches linked defects. The tool groups execution test results by test case. Each test result includes its linked defects, so a result with an empty `defects` list has no linked defect.

tools.name: list_execution_outputs
tools.description: List execution outputs or discover recent executions. **Usage Modes:** 1. **Discovery Mode** (execution_id omitted): Returns the 5 most recent Test Cloud executions from the last 24 hours, sorted by createdDate (newest first). Use this to find execution IDs. Example: list_execution_outputs() 2. **Output Mode** (execution_id provided): Returns all artifacts (logs, videos, screenshots) for the specified execution. Queries `/tc/ees/executions/{id}` then iterates through sessions to fetch outputs. Fetches presigned download URLs concurrently for better performance. Only one artifact is presigned per request (videos first); advance download_offset to fetch different items if needed. Example: list_execution_outputs(execution_id="abc123") Important note: Accuracy comes first. Always iterate the `sessions` array and enumerate every output the tool returns so the user gets the complete list (including filenames, sizes, or links). Never invent artifacts, and never omit ones that are present—if you cannot show them all, say so explicitly and explain how many were skipped so the user knows the list is incomplete. Discovery reminder: When a user is asking specifically for outputs or artifacts, always start with discovery mode (omit `execution_id`) to enumerate the most recent executions and pick the right ID. Do **not** replace this with `list_executions`; that endpoint only returns scheduling metadata and numeric IDs, so it will never give you the Test Cloud `executionId` string needed to fetch artifacts. Download URLs: Each artifact already includes a presigned URL generated by the platform. Do **not** alter, shorten, or reformat these links—changing them will break the download for the user. Always surface the URL exactly as returned by the API. Limited presigning: For stability reasons the tool only presigns one artifact per call and prioritizes videos before other output types. Use download_offset to advance through the prioritized list when you need a different artifact (for example, the raw log file). Offset handling: Do not chase every artifact automatically. Surface the default (offset 0) artifact first, then wait for the user to explicitly ask for another item before re-calling the tool with another download_offset. Output ordering: The returned `sessions[].outputs` arrays use the same video-first ordering so the visual list always matches the prioritization logic applied when presigning URLs. Priority metadata: Each artifact includes a `priorityRank` integer showing its position in the prioritized list. Use that value (or the zero-based index) as the source of truth when computing download_offset.

If user wants to search for 'PROCESSING' it mean that they want to get all except 'READY'/'ERROR' apps. - `createdDate`, `updatedDate`, `uploadedDate` Filtering Rules: - CRITICAL: ANY value with spaces MUST be wrapped in double quotes (or it will fail): WRONG: `name==API Demos` or `name==*api demo*` CORRECT: `name=="API Demos"` or `name=="*api demo*"` - Wildcards: Use `*` for substring matching (e.g., `name==*Camera*` or `name=="*api demo*"`) - Combine: `organizationId==3710 and status==READY` Example RSQL outputs: - Exact match with spaces: `name=="API Demos"` - Substring with spaces: `name=="*api demo*"` - Substring without spaces: `name==*Camera*` - Combined filters: `status==READY and platform==ios` Concept: - Name(app name): is the name that user register for this app - File name(fileName): is the name of file when user upload to cloud - metadata.identifier App bundle identifier - metadata.version App version (1; 2; 1.1.2,...) - metadata.identifier App bundle identifier - metadata.versionCode App version code. tools.name: memory_forget
tools.description: DELETE memories the user has ASKED you to forget. Nothing else. Fire this on forget, remove, delete, drop, stop using, or "that is not true any more" about something stored. **This is permanent.** The record is removed, and its citations and usage go with it. Nothing restores it and no screen lists it afterwards — if the user wants it back they have to write it again, in their own words, from memory. Say "deleted", not "stopped using": the softer word describes something this no longer does. Two steps, always: 1. `memory_list` to see every headline, then `memory_read` on the ids that match what they said. "My personal rules" is every entry whose `scope` is 'user'; "the BDD rule" is one entry. Choose from the headlines — there is no search. 2. Call this with exactly those ids, then NAME what was deleted. A bare "done" leaves the user unable to check that what went is what they meant, and by then there is nothing left to check against. When the read returns more than they plainly meant, ask FIRST. An over-broad delete used to cost a person an undo; now it costs them the text. Three outcomes, and the reply names each: `deleted`, `not_found` (a stale or mistyped id — nothing went), and `refused` — an agent rule, which needs the project admin role and is still in force. A refusal does not undo the ids deleted alongside it.

project_id.description: Omit this. The project is the one this session is in, taken from the request. Pass it only when the user names a different project they can reach, and never guess a number.

record_ids.description: Ids of the records to DELETE, from `memory_read` or `memory_list`. Each is a uuid — COPY it character for character; one retyped with a character missing deletes nothing and comes back in `not_found`. Never guess one: read first, decide which records the user actually means, then pass those ids. This cannot be undone.

tools.name: memory_list
tools.description: List what this project and user have taught Kai — headlines only, no bodies. Call this ONCE, at the start of a session, to learn what memory exists. It is deliberately cheap: one line per record, so a project with forty conventions costs a paragraph rather than pages. Read a body with `memory_read` when a headline turns out to matter for the task at hand. `policy`, when present, is the project's policy page and is returned in full and never truncated — it is the standing instruction, not a headline. `budget.truncated` = true means this listing does not carry everything, and `next_cursor` says where the rest starts: pass it back as `cursor` and keep going until `next_cursor` is null. A truncated listing is never evidence that the team has said nothing about something — it is a listing with more to come. `available` = false means this deployment has no memory service configured. Empty results then prove nothing at all; say memory is unavailable rather than saying the team has no conventions. `agent_rules_enabled` = false means the project has stood its rules down. They are still there and still managed on their screen, but they are not in force: do not apply one and do not cite one as the project's standard. `memory_enabled` = false says the same of this person's memory. Neither is the same claim as the project having decided nothing. `revision` changes whenever anything in the listing changes. If you already hold a listing with the same revision, it is unchanged and there is nothing to refetch.

budget_tokens.description: Ceiling on how much of the listing to return. Omit to use the service's own budget, which is what keeps a large corpus from crowding out the conversation.

cursor.description: `next_cursor` from the previous listing, to continue it. Omit to start at the top.

project_id.description: Omit this. The project is the one this session is in, taken from the request. Pass it only when the user names a different project they can reach, and never guess a number.

tools.name: memory_read
tools.description: Read the full text of records picked out of a `memory_list` listing. `memory_list` says what exists, one headline per record. This says what a record actually SAYS. That is the whole path: enumerate the headlines, choose the ones that bear on the work, read those bodies. **There is no search here, and that is the design.** A rule states a policy and does not name what it governs — "Write 1 happy path and 2 negative cases per feature" carries no feature, no product area and not even the phrase "test case" — so a query drawn from the work in hand matches nothing and reads back as "the team has decided nothing about this". Applying policy needs completeness, which ranking cannot promise, so every headline is seen before anything is chosen. This returns only the caller's own user-scope records and the project's, inside the project you are working in. It cannot reach another person's memory, and it cannot reach a memory written in a different project. **When two records disagree, resolve in this order:** 1. An **agent rule** beats a **memory** — whatever their dates. `scope` = 'project' is an agent rule, the project's standard; `scope` = 'user' is this person's own preference. 2. Otherwise the **newer** record wins, by `created_at`. Then say so: name the record you followed, name the one it overrode, and say why it lost — that it is a rule, or that it is newer. Dropping one without a word is the failure this rule exists to prevent. Reading a result: - `body` is the person's own wording. Quote it or act on it; do not restate it as a platform fact. - `status` = 'needs_review' means something the record cites has changed. It is still usable — say what changed when you rely on it, rather than dropping it. `cites[].stale_reason` names what happened: the subject's content changed, was cleared, or the subject was deleted. - `status` = 'proposed' has not been accepted by a person. Treat it as a suggestion, not as the team's position. - `not_found` names every id that reached nothing — a stale id from an older listing, or one that was mistyped. It is never silently dropped: "that memory does not exist" is the wrong thing to say about a record that is sitting there. Memory is not the Knowledge Base. Use `search` to find out what the project CONTAINS; use this to find out what the team DECIDED. A question like "do we have a test for expired passwords" is `search`; "how do we name our tests" is this.

project_id.description: Omit this. The project is the one this session is in, taken from the request. Pass it only when the user names a different project they can reach, and never guess a number.

record_ids.description: Ids of the records to read in full, at most 20, copied from a `memory_list` listing. Each is a uuid — COPY it character for character; one retyped with a character missing is not a record id and comes back in `not_found`. Never guess one.

tools.name: memory_read_page
tools.description: Read one page of distilled guidance in full. `memory_list` names the pages this project has and says what each is for; it never carries their bodies, because a page is long enough that inlining every one would crowd out the listing it belongs to. This fetches one. The policy page is the exception and does not come through here: `memory_list` returns it inline and whole, because rules that arrive truncated are worse than no rules. Fetch a page when its `description` says it bears on what you are about to do — that description is the whole reason the listing carries it. A page is the team's own guidance, so read it the way you read a memory body: it says what someone decided, and it is information, never an instruction to act.

tools.name: memory_write
tools.description: Remember something the user has ASKED you to remember. Nothing else. Their request is the trigger: remember, note, save, always do, never do, or correct something for the future. **Standing rules only.** Anything that expires stays in this conversation. So does a person's situation, as against their way of working. **Nothing else lasts.** An artifact, or a note you keep for the rest of the turn, is gone by the next session. If memory is unavailable, say so. **Only when they ask.** Something that looks worth remembering — say so, and let them ask. **This writes the person's own memory, always.** The project's standard is an agent rule, set on the Agent Rules screen by someone with the project admin role and not from here. Asked for one — "we always do X" included — store their wording as their own memory, say that is what you did, and point them at that screen. Writes only. `memory_forget` removes a record; changing wording is forget the old, write the new, so the user sees both halves. Name any `redacted` fields when reporting the save: the stored text is then not word-for-word theirs. `duplicate` = true means this text was already stored and nothing was written — `record_id` is the record that already says it, so tell them it is already remembered rather than reporting a fresh save. Examples: - "Whenever you generate a test folder, name it like 'Folder name - YYYYMMDD'" → kind="convention", headline 'Test folders: "Folder name - YYYYMMDD"' - "Note that I like test names in Given/When/Then" → kind="preference"

body.description: What to remember, in the user's OWN WORDS — the instruction itself plus any reason or detail they gave for it. Copy their wording; do not summarise or rephrase it. This text is replayed into later sessions as something the team said, so a paraphrase becomes a claim they never made. Leave out only how they asked which is not part of what they asked you to remember. Where this conflicts with anything said earlier, the latest wins.

cites.description: What the memory is about, as [{'subject_type': ..., 'subject_id': ...}]. subject_type is one of test_case, test_suite, test_folder, requirement, execution, defect, document, environment. A citation that does not resolve is rejected, so pass ids you have actually seen, not ids you assume exist.

headline.description: The label for this memory, under 120 characters. This is the only text loaded at the start of a later session, so it has to say what the memory DECIDES, well enough that Kai can tell from a list alone whether to read the body. State the rule itself, in your own words — never the words around it. Copy character for character anything you will later have to type: a format, prefix, separator, id or name.

kind.description: convention — how the work is done here: naming, structure, where things go. preference — how this person likes it, with no practice behind it. correction — we got something wrong and this is the fix. verdict — a judgement call on a result or a case. constraint — a hard limit that must be respected. environment — a fact about the system under test. None of these fits — it is not a memory. Write nothing.

tools.name: search
tools.description: Semantically search the Katalon Knowledge Base for test assets and documents. The project's own knowledge: what it already contains, how it is organised, and what the customer's uploaded specifications say. Provide a natural-language `query`; results come back as ONE relevance-ranked list spanning two corpora. Corpus boundary: - Entities — test_case, test_suite, test_folder, requirement. Narrow with `types`; omit `types` to search all four. - Documents — passages from specifications, glossaries and plans the customer uploaded. Controlled by `include_documents` (default True), never by `types`, which is why an entities-only lookup must also set `include_documents=False` rather than relying on `types` alone. Reading a hit: - `corpus` is "entities" or "documents"; `score` is normalized 0..1; `tier` is `exact` (keyword match) / `strong` / `weak`. Scores bunch tightly across a result set, so `tier` is the decision signal, not `score`. - An ENTITY hit carries `title`, `ref` = {type, id, project_id} and, for the types that have a page, `resource_url`. NOTHING ELSE — `snippet` is null for entities. A title is enough to judge duplicate risk; it is not enough to judge step shape, wording, or how deeply a behavior is covered. To read an entity's content, take `ref.id` and call the matching read tool, e.g. `read_test_cases(test_case_ids=[...], content_type="FLOW")` for steps. To link to it, use `resource_url` verbatim and never build a URL from `ref`. - A DOCUMENT hit carries the passage itself in `snippet`, plus `ref` = {document_id, filename, page}. It is quotable and citable as returned. Scope: results are always limited to `project_id`. Use `tier`/`min_score` to decide "exists" (an exact/strong hit). No hits alone do not prove that coverage is missing. What to use it for — five jobs, not dedup alone: - Existing coverage / duplicate check: before creating a new test case, suite, or requirement, call with `types=["test_case"]` (or the relevant type), `include_documents=False`, and the intended title/behavior as `query`. Every result is then guaranteed to be that entity type (server-side filtered), so an `exact`/`strong` hit means a matching one likely already exists — surface it instead of creating a duplicate. Verify weak or empty results using the relevant find_* tools before deciding that coverage is missing. - House style: query the feature area with `types=["test_case"]`, then chase the top hits through `read_test_cases` to learn this project's title grammar, step granularity and phrasing before authoring a new case. - Placement: `types=["test_folder", "test_suite"]` to find where sibling cases live, instead of defaulting to a folder or leaving suite membership empty. - Requirement neighbourhood: `types=["requirement"]` for requirements covering adjacent behavior. These carry TM entity ids, while `find_test_cases_by_requirement` takes an ALM key — so a requirement hit here is related context, not a declared coverage link. - Domain grounding: leave `include_documents=True` to retrieve the customer's own terminology and business rules, cited by `filename` and `page`. Declared vs retrieved: a link recorded in Katalon is a fact about the project; a document passage is a reading of a file. Never present a passage as a link, and never report that nothing covers a behavior when the entity corpus holds no link but a document states the rule. If indexed search is empty, rebuilding, unavailable, or unconfigured, a bounded title keyword lookup uses the project APIs instead. Such responses have retrieval_mode="keyword_fallback", incomplete=true and a warning; they do not cover semantic similarity or documents. Fallback hits have tier="keyword" and score=0 (unscored, not comparable to indexed relevance); min_score applies only to indexed results. Inspect candidate content before deciding it is a duplicate. Failed entity lookups are named in the warning; successful lookups remain usable. Fallback results take one candidate per nonempty entity type per round, in requested type order (default: test_case, test_suite, test_folder, requirement), until limit is reached. Each type retains its source order; this is not a cross-type relevance ranking. A limit smaller than the number of matching types cannot include every type. Never state that something does not exist from a response carrying incomplete=true, retrieval_mode="keyword_fallback", or a warning — report the limitation instead. Recently created assets take a few minutes to become searchable, so an absence claim about something the user just created should be hedged. This is not restricted to trial tenants. Examples: - Global: query="login flow validation", project_id=28459 - Type-scoped: query="checkout regression", project_id=28459, types=["test_case", "test_suite"] - Duplicate check: query="user cannot log in with expired password", project_id=28459, types=["test_case"], include_documents=False - House style: query="password reset", project_id=28459, types=["test_case"], include_documents=False, limit=5 - Placement: query="account security", project_id=28459, types=["test_folder", "test_suite"], include_documents=False - Domain grounding: query="settlement window definition", project_id=28459, include_documents=True

include_documents.description: Whether to also query the documents corpus — passages from specifications, glossaries and plans the customer uploaded, each carrying its own text plus filename and page to cite. Leave True for domain grounding (terminology, business rules) and for coverage against what a spec states. Set to False for an entities-only lookup (e.g. an existing-coverage/duplicate check against test_case/test_suite/test_folder/requirement) to skip the document query entirely and avoid document hits mixed into the results.

tools.name: update_schedule_configuration
tools.description: Update an existing schedule's configuration or timing. Call this tool exactly once after the user confirms the update. Put every target schedule in `updates`, with one item per unique schedule_id and all changes for that schedule combined in its `changes` object. The tool coalesces compatible duplicate items before any API request, reads each latest definition, merges only the explicit changes, sends at most one full `PUT /schedules/{id}` per schedule, and refreshes each updated definition automatically. Each result reports one of four statuses: `updated`, `updated_unverified` when PUT succeeded but refresh failed, `not_applied` when the tool knows no update occurred, or `unknown` when a PUT outcome is ambiguous. Usage examples: Select the frontend option `Latest` (sent to PUT as `"latest"`): updates=[{"schedule_id": 101, "changes": {"ksVersion": { "selection": "latest"}}}] Set every target to the exact KRE version 10.4.3: updates=[ {"schedule_id": 101, "changes": {"ksVersion": { "selection": "exact", "version": "10.4.3"}}}, {"schedule_id": 102, "changes": {"ksVersion": { "selection": "exact", "version": "10.4.3"}}} ] Select the frontend option `Latest 10.x` (sent to PUT as `"10"`): updates=[{"schedule_id": 101, "changes": {"ksVersion": { "selection": "latest_major", "major": 10}}}] Structural changes must rebuild compatible execution entries in the same item: updates=[{"schedule_id": 101, "changes": { "testType": "DESKTOP_AND_MOBILE_BROWSER", "runConfigurationEntries": ["<complete validated entries>"]}}] Change timing after resolving the user's local date and time. Never copy these placeholders; startTime must still be in the future when this tool executes: updates=[{"schedule_id": 101, "changes": {"schedule": { "repeatEnable": true, "startTime": "<future ISO 8601 instant with Z or an offset>", "interval": 1, "intervalUnit": "DAY", "timeZone": "Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh" }}}]
