ksVersion.description: KRE selection matching the frontend dropdown. Always send exactly one of these object shapes: {"selection":"latest"}; {"selection":"latest_major","major":10}; or {"selection":"exact","version":"10.4.3"}. The tool converts them to the PUT ksVersion values "latest", "10", and "10.4.3" respectively. The update tool validates latest_major and exact values against the same dynamic release feed used by the frontend before it updates any schedule. Never pass ksVersion as a bare string, never copy a UI label such as 'Latest 10.x', and never infer a KRE change when the user did not request it.

maxCloudParallelSessions.description: Maximum cloud parallel sessions requested by the user. The tool merges this value into the full parallelConfiguration sent to the API.

name.description: New non-empty schedule name. Include only when the user asks to rename it.

privateLocalTesting.description: Explicit private local testing change. Never infer this from another schedule or include it for an unrelated update.

repositoryId.description: AUTOMATION_COMMAND only: call list_repositories and copy the selected repository's numeric id. Changing it requires a compatible complete runConfigurationEntries replacement in the same item. For AUTOMATION_UI, use each entry's testProjectId and omit this top-level field. Never invent the ID.

runConfigurationEntries.description: Complete replacement execution-target entries. Resolve repositories with list_repositories; suites with find_test_suites; collections and ordered members with find_test_suite_collections(collection_id=...); profiles with find_execution_profiles; TestCloud browsers/devices with list_test_cloud_environments; local agents with list_test_cloud_agents; and mobile apps with list_test_cloud_apps. Copy exact response values and never invent IDs or catalog strings. TEST_SUITE requires a positive entityId and at least one configuration; profileId is additionally required for effective AUTOMATION_UI schedules and omitted for MANUAL. TEST_SUITE_COLLECTION requires a positive entityId, executionMode, and member TEST_SUITE entries. KATALON_COMMAND and KATALON_GENERIC_COMMAND require a non-empty command and at least one configuration, and may use entityId 0; KATALON_GENERIC_COMMAND supports LOCAL_AGENT configurations only. Include only when the user asks to change execution targets or when rebuilding a structural field.

schedule.description: Complete timing replacement accepted by the schedule API. Include only when the user explicitly asks to change timing. Read the current schedule and copy exact required timing fields when they are available, but never infer timeZone from startTime or a Z suffix. If read_schedule_detail omits timeZone and the user did not provide it, ask for the IANA timeZone and do not call update yet. Use top-level activeStatus for activation or deactivation; a status-only update must omit schedule. The tool preserves the current scheduler active value internally for timing-only updates. startTime must resolve to a future timezone-aware instant and timeZone must be an IANA ID. For recurring schedules include interval and intervalUnit, plus days for WEEK; endTime is optional but must be after startTime. For one-time schedules omit endTime, interval, intervalUnit, and days. Never send the read-only schedulers projection.

testType.description: Structural test type selected in the frontend. Changing it requires a compatible complete runConfigurationEntries replacement in the same item. The writable API field is testType; testRunType is a deprecated compatibility alias read only when testType is absent.

timeOut.description: New timeout in minutes, from 10 through 999 inclusive, matching the frontend. Include only when explicitly requested.

visualTestingConfiguration.description: Complete visual testing configuration replacement. Include only when the user explicitly asks to change visual testing.

xrayImportReportType.description: New Xray import report type. Include only when explicitly requested.

ScheduleConfigurationUpdate.description: One schedule and its explicit changes inside a batch update.

changes.description: Only settings explicitly requested by the user for this schedule. Omit unchanged, inferred, and defaulted fields.

schedule_id.description: Schedule identifier. Include each schedule_id only once in the updates array; put all requested changes for that schedule in the same item.

ScheduleTimingChange.description: Complete writable timing body matching frontend and backend rules.

days.description: Selected weekdays. Required and non-empty for WEEK recurrence; omit it for a one-time schedule.

endTime.description: Optional end instant for a repeating schedule. If provided, it must be timezone-aware and strictly after startTime. Omit it for a one-time schedule.

interval.description: Repeat interval. Required when repeatEnable is true; omit it for a one-time schedule.

intervalUnit.description: Repeat unit selected in the frontend. Required when repeatEnable is true; omit it for a one-time schedule.

repeatEnable.description: Whether the schedule repeats. When false, omit endTime, interval, intervalUnit, and days, matching the frontend PUT payload.

startTime.description: Next start as a future, timezone-aware ISO 8601 instant with Z or an explicit UTC offset. Resolve the user's local date and time before calling; never reuse an already-past startTime from the current schedule.

timeZone.description: IANA timezone ID used by the frontend and backend, for example Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh. Do not send a display label or numeric offset such as UTC+7.

VisualTestingConfigurationChange.description: Complete visual-testing configuration accepted by the schedule API.

baselineCollectionGroupOrder.description: Preserve the existing value from read_schedule_detail or use an explicit user-supplied value. No installed MCP discovery tool lists baseline collection groups; do not invent it.

enabled.description: Enable or disable visual testing only when the user explicitly requests that change. Enabling with a baseline requires a valid existing baselineCollectionGroupOrder.

project_id.description: ID of the project. If not in context, call list_projects to find available options.

updates.description: Every schedule update in the user's confirmed request. Call this tool exactly once for the entire request and include every target schedule in this array; do not invoke the tool separately for individual schedules. For each item, include only explicitly requested changes and combine all changes for one schedule_id into that single item. Do not copy a response from read_schedule_detail or include unchanged, inferred, or defaulted fields, except for the complete schedule object required for a timing change as described below. Use testType; do not also send the deprecated testRunType compatibility alias. For ksVersion, send exactly one structured shape: {selection:'latest'}, {selection:'latest_major', major:10}, or {selection:'exact', version:'10.4.3'}. These map to PUT values 'latest', '10', and '10.4.3'. The tool verifies latest_major and exact selections against the same dynamic KRE release feed used by the frontend before updating any schedule. Never pass ksVersion as a bare string or copy a UI label such as 'Latest 10.x'. Use maxCloudParallelSessions for the user's Max Cloud Parallel Sessions value. For a status-only change, send only top-level activeStatus; do not send schedule or copy current timing. For any timing change, send one complete schedule object: startTime must be a future ISO 8601 instant with Z or an offset and timeZone must be an IANA ID. Do not put active inside schedule; use activeStatus when the user also requests a status change. The tool preserves the current active value internally, or lets the backend activate a newly created parent scheduler. Read current timing fields first, but never infer timeZone from startTime or a Z suffix. If read_schedule_detail omits timeZone and the user did not supply it, ask for the IANA timeZone and do not call update yet. Recurring schedules require interval and intervalUnit, plus days for WEEK; one-time schedules must omit recurrence-only fields. name must be non-empty and timeOut must be from 10 through 999. configType, testType, and repositoryId are structural: never change one alone; send a compatible complete runConfigurationEntries replacement in the same schedule item. Lookup routing before calling this tool: use read_schedule_detail for the current schedule; list_repositories for repository IDs; find_test_suites for suite IDs; find_test_suite_collections(collection_id=...) for collection IDs and ordered members; find_execution_profiles for profile IDs/names; list_test_cloud_environments for TestCloud desktop and shared mobile OS, browser, version, and device values; preserve an existing private-cloud device or use exact user-provided private device values because no installed lookup tool exposes new private devices; list_test_cloud_agents for LOCAL_AGENT IDs; list_test_cloud_apps for MOBILE_NATIVE app values; and list_test_cloud_tunnels followed by build_private_local_testing_config for a new private-local-testing configuration. Copy exact response fields; do not invent IDs, dynamic values, or UI labels. If a lookup returns zero matches, do not update that field; if it returns multiple plausible matches, ask the user to choose instead of selecting the first result. KATALON_GENERIC_COMMAND supports LOCAL_AGENT configurations only. Frontend catalog/display fields agentName, isAgentActive, deviceFamily, appPlatform, appCodeVersion, and testCloudExecutionType are not writable RunConfigurationEnvironment fields. Use them only as lookup filters when applicable; never translate them into browser, os, executionType, or a different writable field, and never put them inside metadata. Metadata accepts typed browserVersionType, devicePool, udid, appVersion, and appVersionCode values. Copy mobile devicePool from the selected unified environment. For private_cloud, preserve udid from the current schedule or use an exact user-provided value because the unified catalog does not expose it; the backend-only devicePoolId is filled from organization context. Copy appVersion and appVersionCode from the selected READY app metadata. testCloudEnvironmentUuid is optional and must never be invented. Never add devicePool merely because the user mentioned deviceFamily. If the user asks to edit a display field directly, explain that it cannot be updated and do not call this tool. There is no installed discovery tool for new schedule custom-field definitions/options or visual baseline groups: use only values already present in read_schedule_detail or explicitly supplied by the user, otherwise do not update that field. Enabling private local testing requires an existing or newly supplied configuration. Enabling True Parallel automatically changes collection execution modes to PARALLEL. When runConfigurationEntries changes, the tool validates every TEST_CLOUD_AGENT environment against the unified TestCloud environment catalog and every appId against the organization-scoped READY app catalog before PUT. A missing or invented catalog value returns not_applied and sends no PUT. The tool reads each current schedule, preserves omitted top-level settings, and constructs the complete PUT payload internally.

tools.name: update_test_cases
tools.description: Update metadata or content of one or more test cases. ## Action reference | Action | Required fields in `test_case_data` | |---|---| | RENAME | `id`, `name` | | UPDATE_STATUS | `id`, `status` | | UPDATE_DESCRIPTION | `id`, `description` | | UPDATE_PRECONDITION | `id`, `preCondition` | | UPDATE_PRIORITY | `id`, `priority` | | UPDATE_AUTOMATION_STATUS | `id`, `automationStatus` | | UPDATE_ASSIGNEE | `id`, `assigneeUUID` | | UPDATE_LINKED_TEST_CASES | `id`, `linkedTestCaseIds` | | REMOVE_LINKED_TEST_CASE | `id`, `removedLinkedTestCaseId` | | UPDATE_CONTENT | `id`, `content` — see step format below | ## UPDATE_CONTENT — step format `content.steps` fully replaces all existing steps — always supply the complete desired step list. If the case has Call Test Case steps you want to keep, you must re-supply them (with their `action`); omitting them drops the call (and the tool rejects a replacement that would silently wipe an existing action). Each step: - `name` (string, required): action to perform - `context` (object, optional): omit entirely if no expected result is needed - `expectedResult` (string, **required if context is present**): what should happen - `data` (string, optional, default `""`): test input data - `action` (object, optional): structured action for automated/AI execution, in addition to name/context. Today only Call Test Case: `{"type": "call", "test_case_id": <id>}` (optional `"version": <n>`). **Common mistake**: do not pass `context: {}` — either omit `context` or include `expectedResult`. ## Examples Update status and automation status in one call: ```json [ {"action": "UPDATE_STATUS", "test_case_data": {"id": 522324, "status": "IN_REVIEW"}}, {"action": "UPDATE_AUTOMATION_STATUS", "test_case_data": {"id": 522324, "automationStatus": "AUTOMATION_CANDIDATE"}} ] ``` Replace all test steps: ```json [ { "action": "UPDATE_CONTENT", "test_case_data": { "id": 522324, "content": { "steps": [ {"name": "Navigate to the login page", "context": {"expectedResult": "Login page is displayed"}}, {"name": "Enter credentials and click Login", "context": {"expectedResult": "Dashboard is shown", "data": "username=admin"}}, {"name": "Verify welcome message", "context": {"expectedResult": "Welcome message shows the user's name"}} ] } } } ] ``` Replace steps where the first reuses a shared test case (Call Test Case): ```json [ { "action": "UPDATE_CONTENT", "test_case_data": { "id": 522324, "content": { "steps": [ {"name": "Login", "context": {"expectedResult": "User is signed in"}, "action": {"type": "call", "test_case_id": 573794}}, {"name": "Verify welcome message", "context": {"expectedResult": "Welcome message shows the user's name"}} ] } } } ] ```

project_id.description: ID of the project. If not in context, call list_projects to find available options.

repository_id.description: ID of the repository (Test Project). If unknown, call list_repositories to find available options.

updates.description: Ordered list of update actions. Each item: {action, test_case_data}. Actions execute sequentially — always batch updates to the same test case in a single call to avoid race conditions.

test_case_data.description: Data object specifying the update action to perform and its associated parameters.

steps.description: List of test steps. Every step has a human-readable 'name' and optional 'context' (expected result + data); a step may additionally carry a structured 'action' for automated execution (e.g. Call Test Case — see CreateTestCaseStep.action). Unique IDs are generated automatically when creating the test case.

items.description: Test case step definition for LLM input - ID will be auto-generated when sending to API.

anyOf.description:
Call Test Case step action — invoke a shared/existing test case.

One concrete kind of step action. New action types will be added as sibling
models discriminated on ``type``; keep this pattern when extending.

test_case_id.description: ID of the shared/existing test case this step should call.

version.description: Pin the call to a specific version of the callee. Omit to always call the callee's latest version.

action.description: Optional structured action attached to the step so an automated executor (e.g. AI Test Runner) can perform it — in ADDITION to the human-readable name/context, not instead of it. Discriminated by `type`; today the only type is 'call' (Call Test Case): set {"type": "call", "test_case_id": <id>} (optionally "version": <n>) when the user asks to 'call test case <id>' or reuse a shared flow (e.g. a common Login). Still fill `name` (e.g. 'Login') and, if known, `context` so manual execution works. Do NOT encode a call as a plain manual step named 'Call test case <id>' with no action — the runner then cannot trigger the referenced case. More action types may be added here in future.

data.description: Data associated with the test step

expectedResult.description: Expected result of the test step

context.description:
Context containing expected result and optional test data.

        Expected format (both fields must be strings):
        {
          "expectedResult": "Description of what should happen",
          "data": "Additional test data (can be empty string)"
        }

        Fill this for manual execution regardless of whether the step also has an
        `action` — a manual tester follows name/expectedResult/data.

name.description: Human-readable label/description of the step (e.g. 'Navigate to Login page'). A manual tester reads this; keep it meaningful even when the step also carries a structured `action`.

version.description: Version of the test case content format

anyOf.description: The name of the test case. Must start with English letters (a-z, A-Z) or numbers (0-9). Can contain spaces and these characters: ( ) . , _ -

name.description: New name for the test case. Leave as None to keep unchanged.

tools.name: update_test_results
tools.description: Record one manual case result or review one existing automated result. MANUAL/RECORD: updates ONE case, not the whole execution or a case list. Supply test_case_id and final case status. For case-only status + image/file, omit steps and pass confirmed artifact_id references in update.evidence. Case status NEVER implies that all steps have that status. steps is a PARTIAL update: send only explicitly requested step changes; omitted steps keep their status, actual_result and evidence. Prefer 1-based step_number for numbered steps; the server resolves the pinned snapshot ID. Alternatively copy an exact step_id unchanged. Do not reconstruct UUIDs or assume read_test_cases(FLOW) represents the execution's pinned version. Only when the user explicitly reports ALL steps' outcomes, use all_steps_status instead of enumerating steps. Do not combine it with steps. Use steps[].evidence only for evidence explicitly associated with that step. On invalid selectors, use the error's ordered allowed_steps to correct only invalid_steps; do not regenerate IDs for unaffected steps. No writes occur for invalid selectors. Other partial/unknown outcomes require inspection. Examples of update (using a resolved test_case_id): Case only: {"test_type":"MANUAL","operation":"RECORD","test_case_id":123,"status":"PASSED"} Step 19 only: {"test_type":"MANUAL","operation":"RECORD","test_case_id":123,"status":"FAILED","steps":[{"step_number":19,"status":"FAILED"}]} All observed steps passed: {"test_type":"MANUAL","operation":"RECORD","test_case_id":123,"status":"PASSED","all_steps_status":"PASSED"} Case evidence: add evidence=[{"artifact_id": confirmed_artifact_id}] to the case-only update. Resolves manual IDs and creates the result on first use. The run must be active and created by the caller (the backend checks the creator, even when a different executor is assigned). Does not end the run, start a runner, retest, or modify test case definitions. Externally AI-executed manual cases remain MANUAL. Only record observed test outcomes. AUTOMATED/REVIEW: supply execution_test_result_id, expected_status, desired_status and a review reason. Requires a completed automation run. This is a human/AI review override, not execution or report import. The legacy API toggles status: never retry unknown outcomes automatically. Avoid simultaneous reviews of the same result from other clients. Cross-mode fields are rejected. No harness or AI model argument is needed. For new evidence, call prepare_artifact_upload, have the client upload the file to the returned URL, then call confirm_artifact_upload. Pass only the confirmed artifact_id in case or step evidence, or reuse an uploaded attachment's artifact_id already provided by Katalon. Never include file bytes in tool arguments. Return values report actual backend readback; partial/unknown are not success.

execution_id.description: Platform test run ID from its URL, not manualExecutionId or a result ID.

all_steps_status.description: Set every step in the pinned run snapshot to this status, resolving IDs server-side. Use only when the user explicitly reports the outcome of all steps. Do not infer from case status. Cannot combine with steps.

environment_id.description: Manual environment ID; required if the run has multiple environments.

evidence.description: Confirmed artifact IDs to attach to the case result, without changing any step. Use for an image/file requested at case level; do not invent a step association.

items.description: Reference to an uploaded attachment; file bytes stay outside tool arguments.

artifact_id.description: For a new file, call prepare_artifact_upload, have the client upload the file to the returned URL, then call confirm_artifact_upload and use the confirmed artifact_id. Reuse an artifact_id already provided by Katalon for an uploaded attachment. Never invent an ID or pass file contents here.

status.description: Final case result only; does not imply any individual step outcome.

steps.description: Partial updates: include only steps explicitly requested. Omitted steps keep their status, actual result and evidence. Omit this list for case-only updates. Cannot combine with all_steps_status.

items.description: Reference to an uploaded attachment; file bytes stay outside tool arguments.

artifact_id.description: For a new file, call prepare_artifact_upload, have the client upload the file to the returned URL, then call confirm_artifact_upload and use the confirmed artifact_id. Reuse an artifact_id already provided by Katalon for an uploaded attachment. Never invent an ID or pass file contents here.

step_id.description: Exact opaque ID from the run snapshot. Copy unchanged; never reconstruct an ID. Prefer step_number when the user names a numbered step. Supply exactly one of step_id or step_number.

step_number.description: 1-based position in this run's pinned test case flow (first step is 1). Server resolves its ID. Supply exactly one of step_number or step_id.

test_case_order.description: Exact sortOrder from the run snapshot; required when the same case occurs multiple times in a suite.

test_suite_id.description: Required if this case occurs in multiple suites.

tools.name: update_test_run
tools.description: Configure, start/resume or end an existing TestPak, including hosted AI. BEFORE START, resolve the user's execution choice. A bare "run this test" or "start this run", even with an execution ID, assigned executor and "use existing pinned cases/configuration", does not select an execution path. Ask ONE question: "Run With AI (recommended, fully autonomous), or manual testing in TestPak?" Include the recommendation in the user-visible question. Wait for a valid answer before proposing or calling START. Do not infer a choice from MANUAL run metadata or this schema's default. The absence of an AI request does NOT select MANUAL. "I am its assigned executor" identifies ownership, not the requested execution path. Explicit "run/start this TestPak" selects MANUAL; explicit Run With AI selects KATALON_AI. Do not ask an AI/manual question when TestPak was explicitly chosen. A recommendation, unknown answer or write approval is not a choice. Use this tool for a TestPak even when read_execution reports stage=RUNNING: it resumes the first unfinished case, not a completed automated execution. Do not use rerun_execution or merely describe a future call for a TestPak START. TestPak is a workspace holding pinned cases, timers, results and evidence for a manual test run. Creating it does not execute its tests. START with MANUAL starts the first unfinished case timer and returns pinned steps and result selectors. Execute using your own browser/computer tools, or guide the human through those steps and wait for actual outcomes if such tools are absent. Honor the user's execution choice: "start/run this TestPak" or "start with TestPak" selects MANUAL; an explicit Run With AI/hosted AI request selects KATALON_AI. TestPak may hold either kind of run, but naming it does not authorize AI execution. If neither path is selected, ask whether the user wants manual TestPak testing or fully autonomous Run With AI, recommend AI for automatic execution, and wait for the answer before proposing START. A run's configType/executionType=MANUAL and saved configuration identify its TestPak container; they do not select human versus AI execution. The schema's default MANUAL is not the user's choice. A write approval for a guessed mode does not replace the execution-choice question. A chat-only client lacking browser tools does not justify choosing AI. Explicit human testing uses MANUAL. If the user explicitly requires local execution but those tools are absent, explain the limitation and resolve an alternative before switching. For MANUAL, return pinned steps and wait for actual observations; do not collect AI browser profiles, launch an AI session, or monitor AI provisioning. Upload real evidence with the prepare/upload/confirm workflow and record observed outcomes using update_test_results; then START the next case. CONFIGURE updates the TestPak's AUT/private access without starting timers, creating an AI session, or changing results. Use a nested configuration: aut_environment_id from read_auts OR the user's default_aut_environment_url, plus the resolved private_local_testing_configuration if needed. This works for human/local TestPak testing too, including an active manual run. Omitted fields preserve saved values. Already-ended runs and runs with hosted AI execution cannot be reconfigured. CONFIGURE has no execution mode or profile. The backend cannot clear a saved AUT ID or a saved free URL, so switching between those choices requires a fresh run. START/MANUAL only selects a pinned case/environment and starts its timer. To change its AUT, CONFIGURE first. browser_profile_mode is AI-only. START/KATALON_AI launches hosted execution of the full pinned run (one Chrome environment on Windows/Linux). Supply the user's browser_profile_mode choice. Optionally pass the same nested configuration; it is saved and confirmed before session creation when it differs from saved configuration. Matching configuration skips the update and AUT lookup. If session creation fails after saving, the error states that configuration remains saved. Reuse choices already collected. An existing AI session is reused; conflicting AUT/private access/profile is blocked. Required after hosted START (new or reused session): call read_manual_ai_session with the returned manual_execution_id and session_id once before reporting AI progress. Generic run/result snapshots do not expose the AI session state; follow the concrete next_actions. Launch does not prove success. Do not also call create_manual_ai_session, which remains for legacy/explicit-subset launches on fresh runs. Your local AI harness uses MANUAL. END closes the entire run, including AI. Terminal FAILED/BLOCKED/SKIPPED are valid outcomes. Unfinished cases block END by default. If the user has not explicitly requested skipping the remaining cases, ask whether they want to skip those cases and wait for their answer. "Close this TestPak" or "end the run" alone does not authorize skipping. Never retry a blocked END with SKIP without that explicit user authorization. Only then use {action: END, unfinished_cases: SKIP}; this also stops hosted AI. Already-ended runs are not reopened; repeated START never retests completed cases or creates another known AI session. On outcome=unknown, inspect backend state before retrying. Render execution_path as a link. Configure a human/local TestPak without executing: update={"action":"CONFIGURE","configuration":{ "default_aut_environment_url":"https://example.com"}} Start manual testing after configuration: update={"action":"START","execution_mode":"MANUAL"} Hosted AI with a URL: update={"action":"START","execution_mode":"KATALON_AI", "browser_profile_mode":"SHARED","configuration":{ "default_aut_environment_url":"https://example.com"}} Close a finished run: update={"action":"END"}

execution_id.description: Platform executionId returned by create_test_run(mode='manual') or list_executions. Do not pass manualExecutionId or the UI order number.

project_id.description: Project ID from list_projects; defaults to the MCP connection project.

update.description: TestPak command: CONFIGURE changes AUT/private access, START executes manually or with hosted AI, END closes. BEFORE START, the user must select a path: explicit TestPak/manual means MANUAL, explicit Run With AI means KATALON_AI. A bare run-this-test request with an ID, assigned executor and saved configuration is unresolved: ask Run With AI (recommended) or manual TestPak and WAIT before this call. No AI request does not imply MANUAL. Run verdict comes from case results and cannot be assigned.

action.description: CONFIGURE updates the TestPak's AUT/private access without executing tests; START begins manual work or hosted AI; END closes the entire run.

browser_profile_mode.description: Required for KATALON_AI START only. SHARED carries browser state between cases; SEPARATE isolates each case. Reuse the user's choice without asking again.

aut_environment_id.description: AUT environment selected from read_auts. Omit to preserve the saved AUT; do not combine with default_aut_environment_url. A run with a saved free URL requires a fresh run for this AUT selection because the backend cannot clear that URL.

default_aut_environment_url.description: User-provided HTTP/HTTPS AUT URL when no configured AUT exists. Omit to preserve the saved URL; do not combine with aut_environment_id.

mode.description: Copy the user's resolved build_private_local_testing_config output.

private_local_testing_configuration.description: Resolved Tunnel/IP Whitelisting choice from build_private_local_testing_config; omit to preserve saved private access.

configuration.description: Required for CONFIGURE. Optional for KATALON_AI START to save and confirm configuration before launch. For manual testing use CONFIGURE, then START/MANUAL. Omit on AI START to preserve saved configuration.

environment_id.description: For MANUAL START only: manual environment ID from the run; required with multiple environments.

execution_mode.description: Resolve the user's execution choice BEFORE START: a bare 'run this test' or 'start this run' with an ID, assigned executor or saved configuration is unresolved. Ask one question: Run With AI (recommended, fully autonomous), or manual testing in TestPak? Include the recommendation in the question shown to the user, then wait for a valid answer. The absence of an AI request is NOT a MANUAL choice; do not default to MANUAL with the reason no autonomous mode was specified. The default MANUAL and configType/executionType=MANUAL do not select a path. Explicit 'run/start this TestPak' or 'start with TestPak' selects MANUAL (case timer and steps), without an AI/manual question; explicit Run With AI/hosted AI selects KATALON_AI (hosted browser). A recommendation, unknown answer or write approval is not a choice. Do not choose AI because the client lacks browser tools. Preserve explicit local execution intent.

execution_test_case_id.description: For MANUAL START only: pinned snapshot case ID; omit to select the running or first unfinished case. Not the repository test case ID.

unfinished_cases.description: For END only: reject unfinished cases by default. Use SKIP only after the user explicitly authorizes skipping remaining cases; closing the run alone does not authorize skipping. SKIP also stops hosted AI.
